newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia wants credit rates at 12-15 pct in 1998.
newsitem.headline: Russia wants credit rates at 12-15 pct in 1998.

text.p: The Russian government's plan to cut the budget deficit, and hence yields on government debt, should facilitate a fall in commercial bank loan rates to 12-15 percent next year, First Deputy Prime Minister Anatoly Chubais said on Tuesday.

"Our task for 1998 is to bring interest rates on untied credits of commercial banks to 12 percent, or 15 percent at most," Chubais told a meeting of the Siberian Accord, which groups officials and businessmen from Siberian regions.

Officials are pinning their hopes for economic recovery on lower interest rates which will make it possible for industry to borrow for investment. At present banks prefer to speculate on financial markets or lend to the government by buying Treasury bills, which currently yield around 30 percent a year.
Rates on commercial bank loans to industry vary widely but bankers said they currently averaged about 45-55 percent.

Chubais said the government would attain its goal of lower rates mainly by pushing down yields on government securities, and this would be done by reducing the budget deficit while continuing the present currency policy and general economic policies.
The budget deficit excluding debt servicing would fall to 2.0 percent of gross domestic product in 1998 from a planned 3.5 percent this year, he said.
"The only way to cut T-bill yields will be to cut the budget deficit and reduce the amount of domestic borrowing," he said.
